exhibits.outcome: Reproducible trials report detection, pre-failure alarms, misses, median delay, and an analytical IID APT window false-alarm probability.
exhibits.limits: Small, fixed-seed synthetic trials; manual thresholds require source-specific deployment justification and do not alter the commissioned monitor above.

exhibits.title: Generate, sign, verify and tamper with real SLH-DSA
exhibits.action: Select one of four SHA-2 SLH-DSA parameter sets, generate a keypair and sign a message, then verify and flip a bit in the signature or message.
exhibits.outcome: Runs noble's keygen/sign/verify, displays measured times and key/signature lengths, and shows verifier acceptance or tamper rejection.
exhibits.limits: Only four SHA-2 parameter sets (128f/128s/256f/256s) are wired; the expandable mechanism diagram is illustrative and is not parsed from the library's actual signature.

exhibits.title: Forge a scaled WOTS+ signature after one-time key reuse
exhibits.section: Forge it yourself — complete WOTS+, checksum included
exhibits.action: Generate the eight-chain teaching key, sign one message and try the forgery search, then sign a different message under the same key and retry.
exhibits.outcome: Counts candidate messages that clear message chains and those blocked by checksum chains; when a reachable new message is found, derives the forged signature by forward hashing and asks the unmodified WOTS+ verifier whether it passes.
exhibits.limits: Complete checksum-chain logic at a deliberately reduced 24-bit digest; rare digest collisions are identified separately, and a finite candidate budget does not guarantee a forgery on every run. This is not a practical break of full-width FIPS 205 WOTS+.

exhibits.title: Compute FORS indices and a reduced forest
exhibits.action: Select a SHA-2 SLH-DSA parameter set, enter a message and click Compute FORS.
exhibits.outcome: Displays the real parameter widths from noble's PARAMS, computes k digest indices via base_2b, hashes reduced trees containing the selected leaves, and visualizes their roots and derived teaching public key.
exhibits.limits: A parallel pedagogical reconstruction, not the internals of the noble signature just produced. The drawn trees stop at height min(a,4), the randomizer and seed are deterministic demo values, and hash-domain details are simplified.

exhibits.title: Test the boundary of independently signed messages
exhibits.action: Add signed messages, verify all, then change message bytes, edit the unsigned author/time, reorder or remove entries, or replace a key and re-sign.
exhibits.outcome: Rechecks the per-entry SLH-DSA signatures and reports whether the present message bytes verify under each supplied key; the exercises show changed bytes fail while unsigned metadata and collection changes can leave remaining signatures valid.
exhibits.limits: The historical Ledger label does not indicate an authenticated append-only ledger: each entry supplies its own key; author, time, ordering, completeness and trusted identity binding are unsigned. Key replacement with re-signing is not a forgery under the original key.

exhibits.title: LSB image embedding and extraction
exhibits.section: Exhibit 2 — LSB Substitution: The Simplest Technique
exhibits.action: Enter a message, optionally select passphrase-based AES-256-GCM encryption, embed it in the cover image, and extract or download the stego PNG.
exhibits.outcome: Displays the altered image, histogram, PSNR, capacity and changed-channel count, then recovers the embedded message or reports a decode error.
exhibits.limits: An educational spatial LSB carrier, not a claim of undetectability; encryption is optional and separate from concealing the message's existence.

exhibits.title: Chi-squared detection of LSB embedding
exhibits.action: Test the original cover and the LSB stego image, or generate a payload-rate detectability curve.
exhibits.outcome: Displays chi-squared statistic, the model's probability-of-embedding value and a threshold verdict for each tested carrier.
exhibits.limits: This specific whole-image histogram test is a heuristic with a chosen threshold; a negative verdict does not establish resistance to other detectors.

exhibits.title: F5-inspired DCT coefficient embedding
exhibits.action: Compute an 8×8 DCT, embed a short message in selected AC coefficient parities, render the inverse transform, and extract from the coefficient stream.
exhibits.outcome: Shows before-and-after coefficient heatmaps, a rendered image, bit capacity status and recovered text from the in-memory DCT state.
exhibits.limits: Raw-image educational DCT workflow, not full F5, JPEG quantization or a proven round-trip through a saved JPEG file.

exhibits.title: Texture-guided versus sequential image embedding
exhibits.action: Compute the Sobel texture map, embed the same message by texture-ranked and sequential placement, then compare the carriers.
exhibits.outcome: Shows residual maps, mean texture and smooth-region fraction at embedding sites, and each carrier's chi-squared verdict.
exhibits.limits: A Sobel-ranked educational simplification inspired by WOW, not WOW or S-UNIWARD; the comparison does not run a machine-learning detector, and either carrier may trigger or evade this chi-squared test.

exhibits.title: Step through a TLS 1.3 full handshake
exhibits.action: Use Step, Back, Auto-play, message selection or New session to inspect the message sequence and live transcript-hash chip.
exhibits.outcome: The page runs fresh X25519, Ed25519, HKDF and Finished checks for an educational session, then shows which secrets and checks correspond to each flight.
exhibits.limits: An educational TLS simulation, not an interoperable network stack: both endpoints run in one JavaScript context, certificate parsing is not X.509, and handshake-key badges do not mean each message was record-encrypted.

exhibits.title: Break the current handshake in two ways
exhibits.action: Choose honest, a flipped ECDHE output, or a modified EncryptedExtensions byte and compare the chain, signature and Finished verifier booleans.
exhibits.outcome: The ECDHE mismatch can leave identity checks valid while Finished fails; altering a transcript byte breaks its transcript-bound signature/MAC checks.
exhibits.limits: These are two selectable faults in a single-session model, not exhaustive TLS attack coverage.

exhibits.title: Compare both sides of X25519 ECDHE
exhibits.action: Inspect Alice's and the server's independently computed shared-secret bytes and repeat with New session.
exhibits.outcome: Different private inputs yield matching 32-byte secrets in an honest run; new ephemeral keys change session material.
exhibits.limits: A matching Diffie-Hellman secret alone does not authenticate the peer.

exhibits.title: Test signatures, trust anchor and MITM strategies
exhibits.action: Pick reuse-server-certificate, attacker-key signature or unchanged relay for the current session and inspect the separate client-acceptance and attacker-secret verdicts.
exhibits.outcome: The model runs the chosen strategy against this session's chain and transcript: a forged signature or untrusted chain is rejected, while unchanged relay gains the attacker no key.
exhibits.limits: The chain is a teaching encoding, not X.509; it omits hostname, validity and revocation checking.

exhibits.title: Inspect a live HKDF key schedule
exhibits.action: Read the current session's early, handshake, master and traffic secrets and expand one HKDF derivation to inspect inputs, label, context and output.
exhibits.outcome: The page displays actual derived bytes; a New session keeps the page-lifetime Ed25519 leaf key while changing X25519-derived secrets.
exhibits.limits: The leaf key persists only for the page lifetime and the no-PSK Early Secret is a protocol constant, not an ephemeral secret.

exhibits.title: Inspect and tamper with an AES-GCM application record
exhibits.action: Compare the application plaintext, per-record nonce, authenticated header and resulting ciphertext/tag with the byte-flip verdict.
exhibits.outcome: A first request decrypts back to its plaintext and a one-byte change fails GCM authentication.
exhibits.limits: The application record is sealed for real; handshake messages shown with encryption-layer badges are not separately sealed into records.

exhibits.title: Derive a ticket PSK and test binder admission
exhibits.section: Act B · Resume and bind the ClientHello
exhibits.action: Switch psk_dhe_ke and psk_ke and flip the ticket identity or binder byte before early data admission.
exhibits.outcome: The page shows the PSK and both schedules, distinguishes ticket AEAD failure from binder failure, and withholds early plaintext when either verification fails.
exhibits.limits: The ticket's opaque server contents are a labeled in-memory teaching format, not a prescribed TLS wire format.

exhibits.title: Leak the server's ticket key against recorded sessions
exhibits.section: Act C · Leak the ticket key
exhibits.action: Press Leak the ticket key and compare recorded psk_ke and psk_dhe_ke sessions.
exhibits.outcome: The model opens the ticket and recovers the PSK: recorded 0-RTT data is readable in both modes, while fresh X25519 protects psk_dhe_ke's resumed 1-RTT record.
exhibits.limits: This is a controlled educational compromise of the in-memory server ticket key, not access to a real server.

exhibits.title: Replay a 0-RTT bill payment across two regions
exhibits.section: Act D · Record and replay a 0-RTT bill payment
exhibits.action: Choose a server admission policy, record the ClientHello and encrypted early record, then replay identical bytes to two modeled regions.
exhibits.outcome: The execution logs/counts reveal that valid binder and ticket do not ensure freshness: the broken policy can execute twice, local replay recording can miss a replay in a second region, and shared single-use state changes admission.
exhibits.limits: This is a two-region in-page model with selected policies and one payment action, not a general proof of a deployment's replay safety.

exhibits.title: Cipher: encrypt and decrypt
exhibits.action: Enter text and a repeating keyword, then switch between encryption and decryption.
exhibits.outcome: The transformed text and per-letter input/key/shift/output strip update, with the first tabula-recta cell highlighted.
exhibits.limits: Classical repeating-keyword cipher, not an OTP or a modern stream cipher.

exhibits.title: Break workbench: Kasiski and index of coincidence
exhibits.action: Select a bundled scenario or paste ciphertext, adjust maximum key length, and choose a candidate period.
exhibits.outcome: Repeated substrings and spacings, factor frequencies, and per-period IoC measurements guide a key-length hypothesis or report insufficient evidence.
exhibits.limits: Short text, non-English text, or long sparse columns can make the statistical diagnosis inconclusive; that does not establish secrecy.

exhibits.title: Column frequency solve and candidate decryption
exhibits.action: Run the solver, inspect chi-squared heatmaps for each Caesar column, override shifts, and use Challenge mode to submit a key or request hints.
exhibits.outcome: The transcript, live plaintext preview, confidence diagnostics, candidate key, and decryption update; bundled answers verify exact key and plaintext when available.
exhibits.limits: English quality is a heuristic, not proof; custom ciphertext has no bundled answer for verification.

exhibits.title: Why Vigenere fails: replay
exhibits.action: Spotlight each repeating-key column and toggle mathematical versus historical explanation.
exhibits.outcome: An aligned KEY example shows each column behaving as a Caesar cipher and repeated plaintext at aligned offsets yielding repeated ciphertext.
exhibits.limits: The replay is a fixed illustrative example; the separate workbench analyzes user ciphertext.

exhibits.title: Tamper the signed prekey signature
exhibits.action: Flip the SPK signature byte or substitute an attacker-signed SPK while Bob's identity key remains in the bundle.
exhibits.outcome: XEdDSA verification fails and the X3DH handshake aborts before deriving a shared secret or sending a message.

exhibits.title: Replace the whole prekey bundle
exhibits.action: Offer a different identity key and its correctly signed prekey, then compare the offered fingerprint with a previously trusted Bob fingerprint.
exhibits.outcome: The signature can remain valid while the identity pin mismatches. The deliberately unpinned continuation lets the attacker derive the same session key and decrypt the first message.
exhibits.limits: The trusted fingerprint is a teaching fixture; real users must authenticate identities independently. The unpinned continuation demonstrates the failure and is not a secure protocol path.

exhibits.title: Drop the optional one-time prekey
exhibits.action: Toggle off Bob's one-time prekey and examine the DH set and status strip.
exhibits.outcome: The fourth DH term is omitted, while Alice and Bob can still derive a matching shared secret.
exhibits.limits: This teaching contrast does not constitute a forward-secrecy proof.

exhibits.title: Corrupt Alice's ephemeral key on the wire
exhibits.action: Flip a byte of the transmitted EK_A public key and follow Bob's derivation and initial-message decryption.
exhibits.outcome: The independently computed secrets diverge and AES-GCM authentication fails at Bob.
exhibits.limits: The initial-message demonstration omits X3DH's identity-key associated data, explicitly disclosed in src/ui.ts:628.
